item.title: Correction · Nancy & Stephen Grand Family House: The map notes said OCII's commission meeting was March 18; OCII's own Resolution No. 10-2014 is dated March 4, 2014, and the notes now say so (and that Citizen Portal is an automated summary, not a primary source). The 2012 parcel recording date now cites the DataSF Parcels record. The record said Family House serves children treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital; OCII's resolution says families of patients primarily treated at UCSF Mission Bay Medical Center, so the summary and notes now use that wording. Founding year, the earlier Judah St. building, nightly capacity, families served and 'low-income-qualified' were removed because no readable cited page states them. The summary's ~92,000 sq ft was replaced by the Assessor's 89,197 sq ft with OCII's planned 96,000 sq ft noted, the Nancy & Stephen Grand name now cites Family House's rooms page, and the milestone no longer calls OCII successor to the 'Mission Bay Redevelopment Agency'. The Wikimedia aerial credit names only the Commons username Firstcultural. The May 2016 opening rests on a UCSF page that blocks automated fetches and remains listed among the record's open questions.
item.description: The map notes said OCII's commission meeting was March 18; OCII's own Resolution No. 10-2014 is dated March 4, 2014, and the notes now say so (and that Citizen Portal is an automated summary, not a primary source). The 2012 parcel recording date now cites the DataSF Parcels record. The record said Family House serves children treated at UCSF Benioff Children's Hospital; OCII's resolution says families of patients primarily treated at UCSF Mission Bay Medical Center, so the summary and notes now use that wording. Founding year, the earlier Judah St. building, nightly capacity, families served and 'low-income-qualified' were removed because no readable cited page states them. The summary's ~92,000 sq ft was replaced by the Assessor's 89,197 sq ft with OCII's planned 96,000 sq ft noted, the Nancy & Stephen Grand name now cites Family House's rooms page, and the milestone no longer calls OCII successor to the 'Mission Bay Redevelopment Agency'. The Wikimedia aerial credit names only the Commons username Firstcultural. The May 2016 opening rests on a UCSF page that blocks automated fetches and remains listed among the record's open questions. Source: OCII Resolution No. 10-2014, 2014-03-04 (https://sfocii.org/files/inline-files/2014010.pdf); DataSF Assessor Historical Secured Property Tax Rolls, parcel 8711227 (https://data.sf.gov/resource/wv5m-vpq2.json?parcel_number=8711227); DataSF Parcels (https://data.sfgov.org/Geographic-Locations-and-Boundaries/Parcels-Active-and-Retired/acdm-wktn); Family House, Rooms (https://familyhouseinc.org/rooms/); UCSF, 2016-05 (https://www.ucsf.edu/news/2016/05/402766/new-family-house-opens-mission-bay).

item.title: Complete · Nancy & Stephen Grand Family House: New Family House building opened in Mission Bay (Family House's history page: "In 2016, the 80-bedroom Nancy and Stephen Grand Family House opened in Mission Bay"; DataSF Assessor year built 2016). The month differs by source: Potrero View (February 2016, before the event) said the house "opens next month", while UCSF's news article "New Family House Opens at Mission Bay", whose web address is dated 2016/05, could not be read (~2016)
